diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Note that $K(\cdot,\cdot)$ and $G(\cdot,\cdot)$ are the kernels of symmetric semi-positive compact integral
operators on $H$ and $L^2([0,T]),$ respectively.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof equates the tail sums of eigenvalues of K and G. These operators are E[T^*T] and E[TT^*] for the random kernel operator T. For a random operator, E[T^*T] and E[TT^*] are not generally isospectral. For example, T=[[ξ,η],[0,0]] with independent mean-zero unit-variance ξ,η gives E[T^*T]=I but E[TT^*]=diag(2,0). Thus the displayed equality of eigenvalue tails is false, and the projection error using V_K cannot be identified with the eigenvalue tail of G.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the required eigenvalue decay directly for the spatial covariance operator K (or otherwise bound the spatial projection error), instead of equating the spectra of K and G.
issues.overall_effect: The hyperbolic data-space dimension result in Lemma lem:added-1 is not established by the given proof; the claimed projection-error bound is unsupported.
issues.title: False equality of eigenvalue tails for K and G in hyperbolic lemma
issues.why_classification: The result may be repairable by a contained argument using K directly, but the existing proof contains a false central equality and therefore does not establish the lemma.

issues.failure_explanation: From the eigenvalue decay λ_j=o(j^{-(p+1)}), the tail sum is only o(k^{-p}). To make the tail sum at most ε^2, the required k is typically Θ(ε^{-2/p}), not o(ε^{-2/p}). The proof does not establish the stronger little-o dimension bound stated in the lemma.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace o(ε^{-2/p}) by O(ε^{-2/p}) in the lemma statement, or add stronger decay assumptions to justify the little-o bound.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised dimension bound for the hyperbolic data space is stronger than what the proof supports.
issues.title: Little-o dimension bound in hyperbolic lemma is unsupported
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the asymptotic notation preserves the qualitative polynomial-dimension result, with no major loss of mathematical content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: by Theorem 5.1 of~\cite{vogel1994stochastic}, $f_N$ is lower semi-continuously convergent almost surely  to $f_O$ on the set $C_k := \{\bc:\|\bc\|=k\}$

issues.failure_explanation: The feasible set {||c||_0=k} is not closed. Sample minimizers can converge to a vector with fewer nonzeros, which is not in the true feasible set and need not minimize f_O. For example, with K=2, k=2, f_O(c)=(c1-1)^2+(c2-1)^2, and f_N(c)=(c1-1)^2+(c2-1/N)^2, the minimizer over ||c||_0=2 is (1,1/N), which converges to (1,0) not in Ψ_O. The proof also invokes a convergence theorem on C_k={||c||=k}, a sphere, not the L0 constraint.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, replace the nonclosed equality L0 constraint by a closed feasible set or add assumptions ensuring the limiting support remains size k and is a true minimizer.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed almost-sure convergence of sample-average minimizers for drift and diffusion coefficient estimation is invalid as stated.
issues.title: Sample average approximation convergence fails for L0 equality constraint
issues.why_classification: The theorem's central convergence guarantee is false as stated, and a complete repair requires new assumptions or a changed feasible-set formulation.

issues.failure_explanation: The decision rule uses Φ^{-1}(p^*) rather than the standard two-sided critical value Φ^{-1}(1-p^*/2). For typical significance levels p^*<0.5, Φ^{-1}(p^*) is negative, making the first inequality meaningless. The two conditions also leave a gap between Φ^{-1}(p^*)/2 and Φ^{-1}(p^*), so the procedure is not well-defined.

failure_location.quote: Then for some significance level $p^* \in (0,1)$, we decide that the diffusion part contains multiplicative noise if $2|Z_N|\geq \Phi^{-1}(p^*)$, and it is only additive if $2|Z_N|<\Phi^{-1}(p^*)/2$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a standard two-sided test, e.g., decide multiplicative if |Z_N| ≥ Φ^{-1}(1-p^*/2) and additive otherwise, with a single consistent threshold.
issues.overall_effect: The proposed statistical test for detecting additive versus multiplicative noise can make incorrect or ill-defined decisions.
issues.title: Incorrect threshold in additive/multiplicative noise test
issues.why_classification: The error is local to the heuristic detection rule and can be fixed by using the standard normal critical value, without affecting the main identification method.
